text: {"lessons":["Repeatedly trimming Stock D at a profit—and later selling a small amount after a very large rise—shows me that taking profits in pieces can be useful, but I should keep a target allocation so I don’t reduce a holding just because it has risen.","I bought Stock B and Stock E after several months without trading; before adding to either, I should check how the purchase fits my diversification and cash plan rather than act on a recent price move.","My account value moved up and down even when I made no trades, so I should review the whole portfolio periodically and judge progress over time, not react to each month’s return."]}
